body.claim: Registering the driver by a name resolved on PATH loses records silently when the wrong binary answers.
body.detail: Two branches that each create the same shard give git an add/add conflict, and git runs the driver to union them. If the codedoc it resolves cannot run `git merge-driver` it exits non-zero, git reports a conflict and writes one side into the working file with no conflict markers. A file that looks intact is one somebody stages, and the other branch is gone with nothing having said so. Observed with a copy one day old that had no git subcommand and reported the same version. The command therefore names the absolute path of the binary that installed it. Anyone tempted to make it relocatable by going back to a bare name should reproduce that merge first.
